create.name: MC Brigitte Schrottenbacher
create.bio:
MC Brigitte Schrottenbacher is a Western Buddhist nun, or mae chi, who was ordained at the Sorn Thawee Meditation Centre in Chachoengsao, Thailand, around 1990. Her first teacher there was the abbot, Phra Acharn Thawee Baladhammo, under whom she trained for five years in the Mahasi style of insight meditation before he asked her to start guiding Western visitors. She later spent seven years learning the Buddho method of the Thai forest tradition with Phra Acharn Sangwahn Khemako, and has also studied with teachers in Bhutan. In 2009 she received a United Nations Women's Day award as an outstanding woman in Buddhism.

For over thirty years she has led silent retreats for foreigners in English and German, teaching on donation. Her monthly week-long courses at Sorn Thawee follow a simple rhythm of guided walking and sitting periods, optional chanting and an evening Dhamma talk with questions, with students keeping the eight precepts. Most years she also spends a few months teaching across Europe. Her talks on the ten perfections and on core Buddhist ideas appear on YouTube and Insight Timer. Alongside teaching she raises support for Thai nuns, students in Nepal and Bhutan, and other social projects.

courses.title: Vipassana Meditation Retreat in Thailand
courses.description: A week-long silent retreat held from the 1st to the 7th of each month in the cooler season at Sorn Thawee Meditation Centre, about an hour from Bangkok. Students stay in individual huts, keep the eight precepts and follow a day of guided walking and sitting with an evening talk; MC Brigitte teaches on donation and the fee covers board and lodging.
courses.price: 3,500 THB (about €90 EUR) for accommodation and meals; teaching by donation

courses.title: November 2026 Retreat at Wat Prayong
courses.description: A five-day retreat in a traditional Thai monastery, Wat Prayong Gittivanaram, guided by MC Brigitte. Days include working meditation, walking and sitting practice, optional chanting with the monks and an evening talk, with simple shared sleeping halls.
